questions.prompt: An administrator changed a VM configuration manually after its original ARM deployment. Which export is intended to capture the current resource configuration?

options.text: Export from the resource group or resource
options.explanation: This generates a template based on the current resource state.

options.text: Export only the original deployment from history
options.explanation: That retrieves the original template, not later manual changes.

options.text: Compile the original Bicep source again
options.explanation: Compilation does not discover drift in Azure.

options.text: Download only the original parameter file
options.explanation: Original inputs do not include subsequent manual changes.

questions.prompt: You have exported an ARM JSON template and want editable Bicep source. Which command performs the conversion?

options.explanation: Decompile converts ARM JSON into a Bicep starting point.
Build compiles Bicep to ARM JSON; it is the opposite direction.
Create deploys the template rather than converting its source.
What-if previews deployment changes; it does not emit Bicep source.

questions.prompt: An exported ARM template will be reused in a new environment. Its required administrator-password input is missing, and a network-interface property contains a hard-coded subnet resource ID from the old environment. The target subnet already exists. Which TWO edits jointly address these two problems? Assume other configuration and permissions are correct.

options.text: Add and reference a secureString password parameter supplied at deployment time.
options.explanation: Export can omit password inputs. A referenced secure parameter supplies the missing input without embedding a literal secret.

options.text: Replace the hard-coded subnet ID with a referenced parameter containing the target subnet ID.
options.explanation: Export can retain environment-specific values. Referencing the new subnet ID directs the NIC to the intended environment.

options.text: Add a subnet ID parameter but leave the NIC property using the old literal ID.
options.explanation: An unused parameter does not change the property; the NIC still references the old subnet.

options.text: Use a new deployment-history name while leaving resource properties unchanged.
options.explanation: A deployment name identifies the deployment record; it supplies neither a missing password nor a replacement subnet reference.
